 <description>En man i 20-årsåldern som misstänks ha hjälpt till vid trippelmordet i Uppsala i april förra året häktas i sin utevaro.       <description>Det føderale politiet FBI etterforsker Nvidia-sjef Jensen Huangs forhold til en kvinne som mistenkes for å ha spionert for Kina, sa president Donald Trump under en pressebriefing mandag kveld.
Trump sa også at Huang «ikke ante» at kvinnen angivelig er en kinesisk spion.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/norge-gir-600-regnskogmillioner-til-brasil-1.18077109</link>
      <description>Klimaminister Sigrun Aasland (Ap) har med en stor sum når hun mandag reiser til åpningen av klimatoppmøtet i Tyrkia.
– Vi har med 600 millioner kroner til Brasil, for de har levert veldig gode resultater på å hindre avskoging i 2025, sier Aasland.
Brasil har det siste året redusert avskogningen til det laveste nivået siden målingene staret for over 40 år siden.
Gjennom den norske regnskogsatsingen gir Norge økonomisk støtte til Brasil når de klarer å redusere avskogingen.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

      <title>Flere skadet etter kraftig jordskjelv sentralt i Japan</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.
(NTB)</description>

      <description>Israels president har gitt opposisjonsleder Gadi Eisenkot i oppdrag å prøve danne regjering.
Hverken partiene som støtter statsminister Benjamin Netanyahu eller partiene som støtter Eisenkot fikk flertall ved valget 27. november.
Netanyahus blokk fikk 53 plasser i Knesset, mens blokken til Eisenkot fikk 48 mandater.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ruud-fikk-revansje-i-paris-_-klar-for-forste-semifinale-siden-mai-1.18076278</link>
      <description>Casper Ruud har storspilt i Paris denne uken. Nå er han klar for semifinale etter seier over Nuno Borges.
Ruuds oppgjør mot portugiseren endte med 7-6 (7-5), 6-4. De to møttes for bare ni dager siden i Basel, og da snudde Borges kampen til seier.
Ruud og Borges kom til semifinalen proppfulle av selvtillit: Ingen har tapt ett sett på veien, og de hadde heller ikke gitt fra seg mer enn fire game i noen av settene.
Ruud spilte kvartfinale i Paris Masters for andre gang. For Borges, som står med én tittel i karrieren (ATP250), var dette første kvartfinale på Masters- eller Grand Slam-nivå.</description>

      <description>President Donald Trump varsler på Truth Social at hans mangeårige rådgiver Stephen Miller blir ny stabssjef i Det hvite hus.

      <description>Politiet opplyser at det har vært en front-mot-front-ulykke på E6 like ved Eidsvoll-tunnelen i sørgående løp.
Ulykken skjedde ved kryss nummer 56 Boksrud. En av bilene kjørte nordover i det sørgående løpet, ifølge politiet.
Det satt en person i hver av bilene. En av dem er bekreftet død, den andre er kritisk skadet.
Det var tåke og svært glatt på stedet da ulykken skjedde.
E6 har midlertidig omkjøring i sørgående retning. Omgjøringen går fra kryss nummer 56 Boksrud via FV1551 Trondheimsveien, og deretter ut på E6 sydgående ved Nebbenes, opplyser politiet.</description>

      <description>Thomas Markle ble pågrepet av føderale agenter i nærheten av Tampa i Florida fredag morgen amerikansk tid.
Han er siktet for forhold knyttet til overgrepsbilder av barn, opplyser kilder med kjennskap til saken til nyhetsbyrået AP.
Tidligere i år ble det kjent at Thomas Markle etterforskes for å besitte overgrepsmateriale på Filippinene. Hertuginne Markles halvbror skal ha funnet overgrepsmaterialet og anmeldt det, ifølge medier.
Meghan Markle har nylig sagt at hun er «dypt fortvilet» over påstandene om at en samling overgrepsbilder av barn skal ha blitt funnet i farens tidligere hjem.
Hun avslørte også at et brev med «urovekkende påstander» om ham ble sendt til politiet i London i 2018.

    <item>
      <title>NFF innfører semiautomatisert offside i Eliteserien</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nff-innforer-semiautomatisert-offside-i-eliteserien-1.18075445</link>
      <description>Det opplyser Fotballforbundet på en pressekonferanse fredag.
– Prisen har kommet ned til et nivå som gjør at muligheten er der, sier generalsekretær Karl-Petter Løken.
Han opplyser at innføringen vil skje i tråd med et dommerløft. NFF bevilger 5,5 millioner kroner i 2027 til dommerløftet, og 3,5 millioner av dem skal få til semiautomatisert offside.
NFF ønsker å øke dette til 7,5 millioner kroner i 2028, og gradvis trappe opp mot 2030.
– Det du har sett med disse linjene blir borte og du får disse visningene med menneskekropper hvor du ser helt tydelig at det er offside. Det er semiautomatisert offside. Det er det ene løftet, sier Løken og fortsetter:
– Det er en utgift som tas én gang og som vil følge oss, og så vil vi trappe opp resten av investeringen i dommerutviklingene i de andre tiltakene i tillegg. Så det blir en gradvis opptrapping, eksempelvis profesjonalisering. Vi starter stille og rolig og så blir det flere og flere.
Dette skjer etter et VAR-oppgjør blant flere toppklubber. Roenborg satt ned et eget utvalg som konkluderte med at «Dagens VAR fungerer for dårlig under norske forhold. De lovte forbedringene har ikke løst hovedutfordringene, og kostnadene er for høye i forhold til kvaliteten».
Utvalget til Rosenborg stilte seg også tvilende til at semiautomatisert offside ville hjelpe VAR i norsk fotball.
– Så det vil være penger ut av vinduet hvis tinget sier nei (til VAR)? spør NRK.
– Vi kommer ikke til å diskutere detaljer i den avtalen, svarer Klaveness.</description>
      <category>Sportsnyheter</category>

A sharp-eyed Victoria police officer helped recover approximately $30,000 worth of jewellery stolen from a downtown business earlier this month.

Just before 5 a.m. on Nov. 2, Victoria police responded to a security alarm at a jewellery store in the 1000-block of Government Street.

Officers arrived to find the business had been broken into and approximately $30,000 worth of jewellery stolen, including one-of-a-kind bracelets and necklaces.

The VicPD Forensic Identification Unit attended to document the scene.

The following day, patrol officers spotted a man suspiciously hiding a bag in some bushes.

When officers checked the bag, they discovered the jewellery stolen from the store the previous day. Police say all the stolen jewellery was recovered and returned to the business owner.

]]> 1360248 Driver who fatally struck cyclist in 2025 handed 2 year driving ban https://cheknews.ca/driver-who-fatally-struck-cyclist-in-2025-handed-2-year-driving-ban-1360197/ Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:46:30 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360197

A driver who ran a red light and killed a cyclist in a Saanich crosswalk in July 2025 has received the maximum penalty for driving without due care and attention: a $2,000 fine and a two-year driving ban.

The post Driver who fatally struck cyclist in 2025 handed 2 year driving ban appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

A driver who ran a red light and killed a cyclist in a Saanich crosswalk in July 2025 has received the maximum penalty for driving without due care and attention: a $2,000 fine and a two-year driving ban.

At sentencing Monday, BC Provincial Court Judge David Silverman acknowledged some may view the sentence as “grossly inadequate,” but explained that “the court’s task is to impose a fit sentence for Mr. Ingram’s inattentive driving,” not the consequence of it.

Ran the red light six second in

It was a clear summer morning on July 28, 2025, as Sylvie Argouarch cycled along the Lochside Trail on her way to work.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

She reached the Quadra intersection and pushed the button. She waited, and when it turned green, she legally rode her bike through the intersection.

Roughly six seconds into the green light and nearly fully through the crosswalk, Ingram, driving a pickup truck, blew through the red light and T-boned her.

Argouarch, an all-around adventurer, mother, partner, and geriatric psychiatrist, died five days later.

At the scene, Ingram told witnesses that he’d been distracted, thinking of his mother, whom he’d just visited in hospital.

Why wasn’t the charge criminal?

BC’s Prosecution Service approved the charge of driving without due care and attention under the Motor Vehicle Act.

Criminal lawyer Michael Mulligan explains that it’s because Ingram’s driving didn’t meet the criminal threshold.

“Most accidents don’t involve a criminal offence. If somebody is simply not paying careful enough attention, even with tragic consequences, that doesn’t necessarily translate into the person committing a crime or even an offence,” said criminal lawyer Michael Mulligan.

“In order for dangerous driving to amount to a criminal offence, the Crown would have to prove that the driving was a marked departure from the standard of care of a normal driver.”

“That would often involve things like speeding, alcohol use, or weaving. And so it would be hard for Crown to prove a criminal offence if all they have is a momentary lapse in attention, like failing to see a light, for example.”

An “appalling” driver’s record

Despite Ingram’s guilty plea and apology to the court, a big factor in the judge’s maximum sentence was Ingram’s severe inattentiveness.

“He was unreactive to a red light for at least six seconds,” said Silverman.

Then there was also Ingram’s “problematic” driving history.

“It is appalling,” said Silverman. “His indifference to basic road safety continues well into his 50s. He has managed to offend in each decade of his driving life.”

Throughout the past four decades, Ingram has 22 driving infractions and six prohibitions, which include a “concerning”, repetitive insistence not to wear a seatbelt.

It’s also a pattern that continued even after he fatally struck a cyclist last year.

Within a year of fatally striking Argouarch, Ingram was handed his ninth ticket for failing to wear his seat belt.

His lawyer had previously told the court that Ingram doesn’t believe that seat belts save lives. At sentencing, Silverman called that “dubious,” which goes against all prevailing wisdom.

Silverman urged Ingram to reconsider what it means to be a safe driver.

2 year ban, possibly more

Mulligan says Ingram faces two years off the road at minimum.

“That does not mean they automatically get their license back. The superintendent of motor vehicles has the discretion to decide if that’s longer if, in their view, their driving record is unsatisfactory, and the argument there being public safety,” said Mulligan.

If Ingram is caught driving while under this ban he could face jail time.

]]> 1360227 Ottawa amends, extends tariff relief program beyond U.S. steel imports https://cheknews.ca/ottawa-amends-extends-tariff-relief-program-beyond-u-s-steel-imports-1360193/ Mon, 09 Nov 2026 23:11:45 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360193

The post Ottawa amends, extends tariff relief program beyond U.S. steel imports appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The federal government is extending its relief program for firms importing tariffed U.S. goods and is changing the mix of goods eligible for those remissions.

Since the early days of Canada’s retaliatory duties against the United States, Ottawa has offered what it calls a temporary remission program to reduce the burden on Canadian firms caught in the tariff crossfire.

The government has routinely extended that program and modified what’s eligible for remissions as it looks to give itself more time to help firms transition away from U.S. suppliers, particularly for steel.

The program’s expiration date will be extended by another year to June 30, 2028. Effective Monday, it will also expand to include non-steel goods used in mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction.

Goods used by public education entities, including those mandated by Indigenous organizations, will be also be eligible for relief.

Certain goods integral to national security, public health and packaging in the agricultural and food and beverage sectors are also exempt.

Canada has maintained retaliatory tariffs on U.S. steel and aluminum imports for most of the trade dispute, but the federal government ramped up its response in September as a new wave of U.S. duties took effect.

The government now imposes counter-tariffs on a range of U.S. goods varying from 15 to 50 per cent.

Ottawa says it’s also planning to exclude goods from the remissions program that can reliably be sourced in Canada.

Certain trailers will be removed from the remissions program on Dec. 1, while aluminum wire and extrusions and paperboard products will be taken out on Feb. 1, 2027.

The federal government’s remissions program has been criticized in the past by the Canadian Steel Producers Association. The group said the relief program removes the pressure on firms to pivot to Canadian suppliers.

Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc argued in a media statement Monday that extending and adjusting these measures strikes the right balance.

“Extending these tariff relief measures gives Canadian companies the support they need today while encouraging greater use of Canadian-made goods and services,” LeBlanc said.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 9, 2026.

]]> 1360170 ‘Doerkson conservative party’ isn’t BC Liberals nor 2024 Conservatives: adviser https://cheknews.ca/doerkson-conservative-party-isnt-bc-liberals-nor-2024-conservatives-adviser-1360184/ Mon, 09 Nov 2026 21:43:31 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360184

The post ‘Doerkson conservative party’ isn’t BC Liberals nor 2024 Conservatives: adviser appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

A B.C. Conservative strategist poised to take a key role in premier-designate Lorne Doerkson’s office says the party has evolved beyond what it was in 2024, without morphing into a new version of the B.C. Liberals.

Angelo Isidorou, who is widely credited as an architect of the party’s rise from political obscurity just a few years ago, has been named Doerkson’s principal secretary after serving as the Conservatives’ executive director and campaign manager.

“I don’t think it’s the BC Liberals, but I also don’t think it’s the old B.C. Conservative Party either,” Isidorou said in an interview.

“I think it’s the Lorne Doerkson conservative party.”

Isidorou said the premier-designate crafted a “positive message” that made the party more appealing, compared to the race in 2024, when Isidorou helped former leader John Rustad bring the party to the brink of power.

Just four years earlier, it had received less than two per cent of the vote. 

“We ran on a populist message in 2024, and it was an aggressive, shall I say, negative populist message,” he said.

“We didn’t give enough people permission to vote for us (in 2024),” he added.

But it was a “false dichotomy” to alternatively think of the party that triumphed with a thumping two-thirds majority in the Oct. 24 snap election as the BC Liberals 2.0, he said. 

The BC Liberals had been a dominant force in B.C. politics for decades, taking economically conservative but socially moderate stances, before imploding ahead of the 2024 election. Many of the most prominent figures in the incoming government — including Doerkson — were first elected as BC Liberals.

“I think (the BC Liberal comparison) is ultimately incorrect, because we didn’t run on a carbon tax,” he said. “It’s not likely we didn’t run on getting rid of DRIPA or SOGI. We did all that. We ran on a Conservative platform.”

He was referring to the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, which Doerkson has vowed to repeal, and a sexual orientation and gender identity framework for schools.

“We have red lines that we care about, and we want you to care about those issues too,” he said. “But ultimately, we are going to prioritize you and your issues.” 

He said “you can call it moderate,” but the party’s policies have not necessarily changed that much. 

“So really, it’s about tone, temperament, and how you present yourself to people, and having some emotional intelligence, and how you communicate.”    

Other appointments were announced on Monday. Allie Blades has been named deputy chief of staff and Shane Mills appointed as executive director of communications.

Dimitri Pantazopoulos was appointed Doerkson’s chief of staff last week.

The appointments are expected to take effect when Doerkson is sworn in as premier later this month.

The Conservatives won a decisive 64 seats in the 93-seat legislature in October’s election.

Isidorou briefly left his strategic roles in the party this year under the leadership of Kerry-Lynne Findlay, but he returned as the campaign’s chief strategist after Findlay resigned ahead of the snap election. 

He said that as a principal secretary, he will do whatever it takes to drive the government’s legislative agenda. “I’m certainly an adviser to the premier and to the chief of staff, and basically I’m put to work, wherever needed.” 

Isidorou said he hasn’t been briefed yet about Doerkson’s early legislative agenda, but B.C. should expect a focus on pocketbook issues. 

“I think the economy is really going to be front and centre,” he said, adding that other top-of-mind issues include keeping hospital emergency rooms open.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 9, 2026.

The Canadian Union of Postal Workers (CUPW) is taking its concerns over Canada Post’s planned elimination of door-to-door mail delivery to local governments, warning the changes could leave municipalities with additional costs and create accessibility challenges for residents.

Kate Holowatiuk, president of CUPW Local 850 Victoria, is set to address Esquimalt council on Monday (Nov. 9), following a similar presentation to Victoria council last month.

The union is pushing for greater public consultation as Canada Post prepares to convert door-to-door delivery to community mailboxes in several Vancouver Island communities beginning in November 2027.

“Community mailbox conversion is being called modernization by Canada Post, but in reality we see it as service cuts,” Holowatiuk told CHEK News.

Holowatiuk says one of the union’s concerns is that municipalities will be left responsible for maintaining the areas surrounding the new mailboxes. While Canada Post would maintain the mailboxes and locks, Holowatiuk says municipalities would be responsible for upkeep of the surrounding sites, including snow removal, garbage collection and vegetation management.

She says some Victoria councillors were unaware of those potential responsibilities when the union raised the issue.

The union is also concerned about how the changes will affect seniors and people with disabilities or mobility challenges who rely on home delivery.

Holowatiuk says Canada Post offers an accommodation program that provides once-weekly delivery to eligible residents, but applicants must go through an approval process that includes disclosing medical information.

“It’s one-fifth of the service that others receive,” she said.

The first conversions in Greater Victoria are expected to affect postal areas beginning with V9A, V9B and V9C, with implementation scheduled for November 2027.

Holowatiuk says other communities between Greater Victoria and Duncan could see similar changes between 2028 and 2030.

She says finding suitable locations for community mailboxes will also be challenging in growing municipalities such as Esquimalt, where development, parking pressures and new cycling infrastructure are already competing for limited space.

The union wants local governments and residents involved in decisions about where mailboxes will be installed to ensure they remain safe and accessible year-round.

Holowatiuk also questioned whether reducing delivery services is the best approach to addressing Canada Post’s financial challenges.

She says the corporation estimates community mailbox conversions will save $2.2 billion over 10 years, while planned postage increases are expected to generate $1.4 billion in additional revenue over two years.

Instead, CUPW wants Canada Post to explore expanding services, including community hubs, while preserving existing post offices.

Holowatiuk says the union has been calling for greater transparency about the conversion plans for more than a year.

“In a nutshell, it’s that the post office belongs to the public and the public should have a say in what that service is and any changes,” she said.

Residents and visitors near the Campbell River may hear warning sirens on Thursday as BC Hydro tests its public warning system.

BC Hydro says the sirens may sound for up to five minutes at a time, multiple times throughout the day.

The warning system is designed to alert people to sudden increases in river flows, which can occur with little warning as part of hydroelectric operations.

When the sirens sound during normal operations, people are advised to immediately move out of the river channel. BC Hydro says the testing is necessary to ensure the warning system at the John Hart facility is working properly.

Temporary signs have been placed along the river to notify the public of the upcoming tests, while permanent safety signs explain what the sirens mean and how to respond.

Investigators believe some of the recovered property may be connected to thefts that were never reported to police.

“We believe many of these items are connected to thefts that may never have been reported to police,” said Insp. Donovan Tait, operations officer with Nanaimo RCMP.

“We encourage anyone working in the forestry, logging, wildfire suppression, construction, or industrial sectors to carefully review the photographs and contact investigators if they recognize any of the recovered items.”

Anyone who believes the items may belong to them is asked to contact Nanaimo RCMP at 250-754-2345.
